unavailable_fields.communication.nccl_wait_vs_wire_separati: No NCCL kernels appear in the torch trace and the task is single-device; nsys is not selected because coverage.json shows 0 unassociated kernels, 0 root-only kernels and 0 ambiguous forward sequences, leaving no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution question for nsys to resolve.
unavailable_fields.gradient_bucket_identity: coverage.json reports backward_associated_kernels=0 and autograd_ranges=0; resnet_inference.py runs under @torch.inference_mode() with no optimizer or backward pass, so no gradient storage exists for native-correlation bucket linking; candidates remain unknown rather than guessed.

unavailable_fields.gpu_ready_and_consumer_completion_times: execution_timeline reports clock alignment bounds for CPU submissions only; GPU readiness and consumer completion may remain unknown and are retained as unknown rather than inferred.
unavailable_fields.cross_rank_clock_alignment: observations.json reports ranks status=not_applicable with reason 'single-device task' and cross_rank.matched=[], so there is no second rank clock to align or subtract against per the clock_policy.

plan.rationale: Frozen objective is latency_ms for batch-32 FP32 NCHW ResNet-18 inference on one leased GPU (GPU-4bead555), with images GPU-resident and TF32/cudnn-benchmark fixed off. The torch collector already ran: coverage.json shows 70 CUDA kernels with all 70 associated, 0 unassociated, 0 backward-associated kernels and 0 autograd ranges, and observations.json marks the communication capability not_applicable for this single-device task, so kernel attribution and communication questions are already closed. The two open questions for minimizing latency are (1) how wall time splits between GPU-busy intervals, CPU submission and synchronization, and (2) how much host dispatch and Python binding overhead the transformers ResNet forward incurs per step. execution_timeline addresses (1) via a separate plain Torch trace with CPU-to-CUDA submit associations, synchronization events and per-device intervals; it does not replace any hook or drive search actions. python_runtime addresses (2) via a warmed cProfile host call trace, interpreted only as a diagnostic of dispatch/binding cost since it perturbs execution. Exclusions: torch is not re-requested because it already ran and ranks top kernels by total time; nsys adds nothing with no overlap, graph-tracing or attribution questions open and cannot separate NCCL waiting from wire transfer (moot: no NCCL); device_telemetry device-wide NVML utilization/PCIe/memory windows cannot attribute single-GPU latency, the workload already records peak_allocated_bytes per sample, and PCIe rates are not per-op bytes; collective_calibration's synthetic full-world SUM allreduce is irrelevant to a single-device inference critical path and is a reference experiment, not a lower bound; candidate_diagnostics is deferred since no capability field or trace evidence currently requires candidate probes beyond the torch kernel ranking.
